sources.entry: qwen-audio-agent - Full-duplex voice interface for AI coding agents. Talk to Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other ACP agents hands-free, with barge-in, spoken permission prompts, async task results read back, and a fully local wake word.

summary.one_liner: A full-duplex realtime voice runtime that lets you talk hands-free to AI coding agents (ACP-based backends such as Qwen Code, OpenCode, Codex, Claude Code) while background tasks run and report back.
summary.what_it_does: The project pairs a realtime voice frontend (cloud services such as Qwen Audio Realtime, OpenAI Realtime, Google Gemini Live, or local options like Hugging Face speech-to-speech) with a backend Agent that executes tasks. Simple questions are answered directly by the voice frontend, while tool use or longer work is delegated to the backend Agent. Users can create multiple asynchronous tasks, check progress or cancel them, and have results returned to the current conversation. It supports barge-in/natural interruption, a WebUI, a terminal TUI, and a desktop floating orb on macOS, Windows, and Linux. The README also mentions a local voice wake word, scheduled reminders, and cross-session memory. Backend Agents reuse their own model configuration, tools, MCP, Skills, and authentication.
use_cases: talk hands-free to a coding agent while it edits code
run background coding tasks and check progress by voice
voice interface for Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode
local voice wake word and speech assistant on desktop
realtime voice conversation with live camera input
scheduled voice reminders and task status updates
how_to_run: qwenaudio tui # Terminal 2: TUI (or: qwenaudio webui)
npm run desktop:build:local # desktop app build on macOS (see desktop docs)
stack: OpenAI Realtime, Google Gemini Live, Hugging Face Speech-to-Speech, MiniCPM-o (optional frontends)
notable: Foreground voice conversation runs in parallel with background Agent tasks, so you can keep talking while work proceeds
Plug-in model for backend Agents: over a dozen ACP-compatible agents plus a bare LLM mode
Replaceable realtime voice frontends behind a Realtime Provider interface
Desktop floating orb with local voice wake word and automatic idle sleep
caveats: Cloud voice frontends require provider API keys and may incur usage costs under their billing rules
Some backend Agents need user configuration or a separate ACP adapter install; some integrations are marked as not yet fully verified (four stars)
AI Passport example is currently half-duplex only; several scenarios (embodied, livestream) are only planned
Desktop builds are provided per platform via npm scripts; Linux build has no signing
